_readme: Teardown manifest for Phase 9. Every row inserted by the Seeder and every Auth user created is recorded here AS IT IS CREATED — appending is part of the insert, not a step afterwards. Teardown deletes exactly what this file lists and nothing else, then verifies the database matches the 'preserved' baseline below.

preserved._note: VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-12 via service_role. This is the exact state teardown must restore.

employees.name: Raywant
employees._status: PRESERVE — this row and its auth.users entry must survive teardown

areas.policy: NOTHING TO PRESERVE — table is empty
areas._finding: The Phase 9 brief stated areas was 'deliberately preserved as configuration'. It is NOT — verified empty. Every area row is therefore Phase 9-created and must be removed at teardown.

products.policy: NOTHING TO PRESERVE — table is empty
products._finding: Same as areas — the brief said preserved, live state is empty. All product rows will be Phase 9-created.

push_subscriptions.policy: preserve rows belonging to employee id 3

baseline_row_counts._verified: 2026-08-12, service_role via PostgREST (Prefer: count=exact). lead_change_log and lead_owner_history counted via an authenticated owner session instead — service_role lacks a SELECT grant on those two (see findings).

excluded_by_decision.plans: User decision 2026-08-12: skip entirely. Zero code references in src/, no UI anywhere, so nothing seeded there could be verified in Phase 7 or appear in the Phase 6 ledger. Phase 5 will still audit its RLS policies.

teardown_notes: stage_history, loss_reasons, lead_owner_history and lead_change_log have NO delete grant and NO delete policy for any role including owner. They can only be emptied from the Supabase SQL Editor, which runs as `postgres` and bypasses RLS. Confirmed in Phase 0.

lead_change_log has ON DELETE CASCADE on lead_id, so deleting a seeded lead removes its change-log rows automatically. stage_history / loss_reasons / lead_owner_history do NOT cascade — delete them explicitly, before the leads they reference.

Deleting an employees row does NOT delete its Supabase Auth login. Orphaned auth.users rows must be removed by hand in the Dashboard — see auth_users_created for the exact list. Never bulk-delete auth.users; that risks removing the owner's own login (1c1c072a-51d5-4027-a592-c79e3c3d46f8).
areas and products were EMPTY at baseline, so teardown must delete every row in both — do not assume any pre-existing configuration survives underneath.

Schema/DESTRUCTIVE_reset_all_data.sql is the blunt fallback (wipes everything except one owner row). It is NOT a migration and must never appear in a run-in-order list. Since areas/products were empty at baseline anyway, that script's end state now matches this manifest's — it is a valid fallback for this particular teardown.
seeder_decisions: Leads carrying a lead_change_log quote_value/order_value correction were inserted with that column NULL and updated immediately afterwards, so the AFTER-UPDATE trigger writes the change row the correction is meant to backdate. Insert-only would have left 75 corrections with no target row.

The author of each value update is the lead author (exec for exec-authored leads, the coordinator for SC-authored ones) so the five SC-entered leads that must remain unlocked keep entered_by_role = NULL.
employees.created_at was backdated to the plan window_start (2026-02-12); the plan does not specify it and the default (today) would misrender "with VIPSAR since" on every Sales Exec Profile.
seed_account_password_location: .env.phase9 -> SEED_USER_PASSWORD (git-ignored). Deliberately NOT stored here: seed_manifest.json is not git-ignored.

post_seed_corrections_applied.run_by: owner, in the Supabase SQL Editor
post_seed_corrections_applied.verified_independently: phase9/verify_seed.mjs — 225/225 rows carry the intended timestamp, 0 still stamped at seeding time, 0 unmatched. changed_by populated on all 225 (no NULLs), so every row is attributable to a real employee on the Day Review.
post_seed_corrections_applied.note: Required because lead_change_log.changed_at is written by an AFTER trigger from DEFAULT now() and the table REVOKEs UPDATE from authenticated — no application session can correct it.
